questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Acid-Base Extraction of Carboxylic Acid and Phenol
questions.question: In an organic laboratory separation of benzoic acid (pKa 4.2), 4-tert-butylphenol (pKa 10.2), and naphthalene in diethyl ether, what reagent selectively extracts ONLY benzoic acid into the aqueous layer?

options.label: A
options.text: Concentrated aqueous NaOH (pH 14).

options.label: B
options.text: Saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate (5% NaHCO₃, pH ~ 8), which deprotonates strong benzoic acid but is too weak to deprotonate phenol.

options.label: C
options.text: Distilled deionized water.

options.label: D
options.text: 6 M Aqueous hydrochloric acid (HCl).

questions.correct_answer: Saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate (5% NaHCO₃, pH ~ 8), which deprotonates strong benzoic acid but is too weak to deprotonate phenol.
questions.explanation: Weak base NaHCO₃ (pKa of H₂CO₃ = 6.35) selectively deprotonates carboxylic acids (pKa ~ 4–5) without deprotonating phenols (pKa ~ 10).

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: When developing a mixture of 1-octanol (polar alcohol) and octanal (moderately polar aldehyde) on a normal-phase silica gel TLC plate using 20% ethyl acetate in hexanes, which compound has the higher Rf value?

options.label: A
options.text: Both compounds remain stuck at the baseline (Rf = 0.0).

options.label: B
options.text: 1-Octanol has the higher Rf value.

options.label: C
options.text: Both compounds have an Rf of 1.0.

options.label: D
options.text: Octanal has the higher Rf value because it forms weaker hydrogen-bonding interactions with the polar silica stationary phase than 1-octanol.

questions.correct_answer: Octanal has the higher Rf value because it forms weaker hydrogen-bonding interactions with the polar silica stationary phase than 1-octanol.
questions.explanation: In normal-phase TLC (polar silica), more polar compounds (alcohols) interact strongly with silica and elute slower (lower Rf); less polar aldehydes elute faster (higher Rf).

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Why is vacuum distillation (reduced pressure, 10 mmHg) preferred over simple atmospheric distillation for isolating high-boiling compounds (bp > 200°C)?

options.label: A
options.text: Vacuum distillation converts liquids directly to solids.

options.label: B
options.text: Vacuum distillation increases the atmospheric pressure.

options.label: C
options.text: Reducing external pressure lowers the boiling point of the liquid, preventing thermal decomposition and charring of heat-sensitive organic compounds.

options.label: D
options.text: Vacuum distillation eliminates the need for heating entirely.

questions.correct_answer: Reducing external pressure lowers the boiling point of the liquid, preventing thermal decomposition and charring of heat-sensitive organic compounds.
questions.explanation: Lowering the system pressure reduces the temperature required for the liquid's vapor pressure to equal external pressure, avoiding pyrolysis.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What is the Atom Economy (AE) of a 100% yielding reaction: A + B → C (where no side products or byproducts are generated)?

options.label: A
options.text: 0% Atom Economy.

options.label: B
options.text: 100% Atom Economy (AE = [MW of desired product / Σ MW of all reactants] × 100% = 100%).

options.label: C
options.text: Dependent on the solvent volume.

options.label: D
options.text: 50% Atom Economy.

questions.correct_answer: 100% Atom Economy (AE = [MW of desired product / Σ MW of all reactants] × 100% = 100%).
questions.explanation: Reactions where all reactant atoms are incorporated into the target product (e.g., Diels-Alder, catalytic hydrogenation) have 100% Atom Economy.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What is the primary thermodynamic criterion for selecting an ideal single solvent for purifying an organic solid by recrystallization?

options.label: A
options.text: The solvent must chemically react with the compound.

options.label: B
options.text: The compound must be equally insoluble at all temperatures.

options.label: C
options.text: The compound must be sparingly soluble in the solvent at room temperature (or cold) but highly soluble at the boiling point of the solvent.

options.label: D
options.text: The compound must be completely soluble at all temperatures.

questions.correct_answer: The compound must be sparingly soluble in the solvent at room temperature (or cold) but highly soluble at the boiling point of the solvent.
questions.explanation: An ideal recrystallization solvent exhibits a steep solubility curve: poor solubility when cold, excellent solubility when hot, allowing pure crystals to grow upon cooling.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: How does a rotary evaporator rapidly remove volatile organic solvents (e.g., CH₂Cl₂ or diethyl ether) from a reaction mixture at low temperatures?

options.label: A
options.text: By freezing the solvent into ice cubes.

options.label: B
options.text: By applying a vacuum to lower the boiling point while rotating the flask to create a thin liquid film with maximized surface area for evaporation.

options.label: C
options.text: By heating the flask with an open flame to 500°C.

options.label: D
options.text: By bubbling chlorine gas through the mixture.

questions.correct_answer: By applying a vacuum to lower the boiling point while rotating the flask to create a thin liquid film with maximized surface area for evaporation.
questions.explanation: Reduced pressure lowers boiling point; rotation spreads a thin film over the inner wall, dramatically accelerating the rate of solvent evaporation.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Steam Distillation of Insoluble Essential Oils
questions.question: Why can water-insoluble, high-boiling organic essential oils (e.g., eugenol, bp 254°C) be distilled with steam below 100°C at 1 atm?

options.label: A
options.text: Eugenol becomes a gas at room temperature.

options.label: B
options.text: In immiscible mixtures, total vapor pressure equals the sum of individual vapor pressures (P_total = P_water + P_oil); boiling occurs when P_total reaches 1 atm (always < 100°C).

options.label: C
options.text: Water chemically dissolves the oil into an ionic solution.

options.label: D
options.text: Steam raises the atmospheric pressure to 10 atm.

questions.correct_answer: In immiscible mixtures, total vapor pressure equals the sum of individual vapor pressures (P_total = P_water + P_oil); boiling occurs when P_total reaches 1 atm (always < 100°C).
questions.explanation: Immiscible liquids boil when the sum of their independent vapor pressures reaches atmospheric pressure, allowing distillation at T < 100°C.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Environmental E-Factor Metric in Green Synthesis
questions.question: In green chemical manufacturing, what does a low Environmental E-Factor (E-Factor = kg total waste / kg desired product) signify?

options.label: A
options.text: A process that cannot be scaled up.

options.label: B
options.text: A process that generates 1000 kg of toxic sludge per gram of product.

options.label: C
options.text: A reaction with zero percent yield.

options.label: D
options.text: A highly efficient, sustainable process that generates minimal waste and byproducts per kilogram of target product produced.

questions.correct_answer: A highly efficient, sustainable process that generates minimal waste and byproducts per kilogram of target product produced.
questions.explanation: The E-Factor measures waste mass produced per mass of product; green, optimized industrial processes strive for E-Factors approaching zero.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Why is a step-gradient of increasing solvent polarity (e.g., pure hexanes → 10% EtOAc → 50% EtOAc) used in silica column chromatography?

options.label: A
options.text: To permanently lock the compounds inside the column.

options.label: B
options.text: To first elute nonpolar impurities rapidly without moving polar target compounds, and then progressively increase solvent strength to elute more polar components cleanly.

options.label: C
options.text: To destroy the silica gel packing.

options.label: D
options.text: To measure the boiling point of the fractions.

questions.correct_answer: To first elute nonpolar impurities rapidly without moving polar target compounds, and then progressively increase solvent strength to elute more polar components cleanly.
questions.explanation: Starting with nonpolar eluent resolves fast-moving components; gradually increasing polarity provides sufficient eluting power to desorb and isolate polar fractions.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What is the chemical function of adding anhydrous magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄) to an organic extraction layer prior to solvent evaporation?

options.label: A
options.text: It neutralizes excess organic bases.

options.label: B
options.text: It forms insoluble crystalline hydrates (MgSO₄·7H₂O), removing residual dissolved and suspended microscopic water droplets from the organic solvent.

options.label: C
options.text: It oxidizes secondary alcohols to ketones.

options.label: D
options.text: It dissolves all organic impurities.

questions.correct_answer: It forms insoluble crystalline hydrates (MgSO₄·7H₂O), removing residual dissolved and suspended microscopic water droplets from the organic solvent.
questions.explanation: Anhydrous inorganic salts coordinate water into solid crystal hydrates, rendering the organic extract completely dry.

options.label: A
options.text: Both compounds remain stuck at the baseline (Rf = 0.0).

options.label: B
options.text: Both compounds have an Rf of 1.0.

options.label: C
options.text: Octanal has the higher Rf value because it forms weaker hydrogen-bonding interactions with the polar silica stationary phase than 1-octanol.

options.label: D
options.text: 1-Octanol has the higher Rf value.

questions.correct_answer: Octanal has the higher Rf value because it forms weaker hydrogen-bonding interactions with the polar silica stationary phase than 1-octanol.
questions.explanation: In normal-phase TLC (polar silica), more polar compounds (alcohols) interact strongly with silica and elute slower (lower Rf); less polar aldehydes elute faster (higher Rf).

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Why is vacuum distillation (reduced pressure, 10 mmHg) preferred over simple atmospheric distillation for isolating high-boiling compounds (bp > 200°C)?

options.label: A
options.text: Vacuum distillation converts liquids directly to solids.

options.label: B
options.text: Reducing external pressure lowers the boiling point of the liquid, preventing thermal decomposition and charring of heat-sensitive organic compounds.

options.label: C
options.text: Vacuum distillation increases the atmospheric pressure.

options.label: D
options.text: Vacuum distillation eliminates the need for heating entirely.

questions.correct_answer: Reducing external pressure lowers the boiling point of the liquid, preventing thermal decomposition and charring of heat-sensitive organic compounds.
questions.explanation: Lowering the system pressure reduces the temperature required for the liquid's vapor pressure to equal external pressure, avoiding pyrolysis.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What is the Atom Economy (AE) of a 100% yielding reaction: A + B → C (where no side products or byproducts are generated)?

options.label: A
options.text: 50% Atom Economy.

options.label: B
options.text: 100% Atom Economy (AE = [MW of desired product / Σ MW of all reactants] × 100% = 100%).

options.label: C
options.text: Dependent on the solvent volume.

options.label: D
options.text: 0% Atom Economy.

questions.correct_answer: 100% Atom Economy (AE = [MW of desired product / Σ MW of all reactants] × 100% = 100%).
questions.explanation: Reactions where all reactant atoms are incorporated into the target product (e.g., Diels-Alder, catalytic hydrogenation) have 100% Atom Economy.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What is the primary thermodynamic criterion for selecting an ideal single solvent for purifying an organic solid by recrystallization?

options.label: A
options.text: The compound must be completely soluble at all temperatures.

options.label: B
options.text: The compound must be sparingly soluble in the solvent at room temperature (or cold) but highly soluble at the boiling point of the solvent.

options.label: C
options.text: The solvent must chemically react with the compound.

options.label: D
options.text: The compound must be equally insoluble at all temperatures.

questions.correct_answer: The compound must be sparingly soluble in the solvent at room temperature (or cold) but highly soluble at the boiling point of the solvent.
questions.explanation: An ideal recrystallization solvent exhibits a steep solubility curve: poor solubility when cold, excellent solubility when hot, allowing pure crystals to grow upon cooling.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: How does a rotary evaporator rapidly remove volatile organic solvents (e.g., CH₂Cl₂ or diethyl ether) from a reaction mixture at low temperatures?

options.label: A
options.text: By applying a vacuum to lower the boiling point while rotating the flask to create a thin liquid film with maximized surface area for evaporation.

options.label: B
options.text: By heating the flask with an open flame to 500°C.

options.label: C
options.text: By freezing the solvent into ice cubes.

options.label: D
options.text: By bubbling chlorine gas through the mixture.

questions.correct_answer: By applying a vacuum to lower the boiling point while rotating the flask to create a thin liquid film with maximized surface area for evaporation.
questions.explanation: Reduced pressure lowers boiling point; rotation spreads a thin film over the inner wall, dramatically accelerating the rate of solvent evaporation.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Steam Distillation of Insoluble Essential Oils
questions.question: Why can water-insoluble, high-boiling organic essential oils (e.g., eugenol, bp 254°C) be distilled with steam below 100°C at 1 atm?

options.label: A
options.text: Steam raises the atmospheric pressure to 10 atm.

options.label: B
options.text: In immiscible mixtures, total vapor pressure equals the sum of individual vapor pressures (P_total = P_water + P_oil); boiling occurs when P_total reaches 1 atm (always < 100°C).

options.label: C
options.text: Eugenol becomes a gas at room temperature.

options.label: D
options.text: Water chemically dissolves the oil into an ionic solution.

questions.correct_answer: In immiscible mixtures, total vapor pressure equals the sum of individual vapor pressures (P_total = P_water + P_oil); boiling occurs when P_total reaches 1 atm (always < 100°C).
questions.explanation: Immiscible liquids boil when the sum of their independent vapor pressures reaches atmospheric pressure, allowing distillation at T < 100°C.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Environmental E-Factor Metric in Green Synthesis
questions.question: In green chemical manufacturing, what does a low Environmental E-Factor (E-Factor = kg total waste / kg desired product) signify?

options.label: A
options.text: A process that cannot be scaled up.

options.label: B
options.text: A highly efficient, sustainable process that generates minimal waste and byproducts per kilogram of target product produced.

options.label: C
options.text: A process that generates 1000 kg of toxic sludge per gram of product.

options.label: D
options.text: A reaction with zero percent yield.

questions.correct_answer: A highly efficient, sustainable process that generates minimal waste and byproducts per kilogram of target product produced.
questions.explanation: The E-Factor measures waste mass produced per mass of product; green, optimized industrial processes strive for E-Factors approaching zero.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: Why is a step-gradient of increasing solvent polarity (e.g., pure hexanes → 10% EtOAc → 50% EtOAc) used in silica column chromatography?

options.label: A
options.text: To permanently lock the compounds inside the column.

options.label: B
options.text: To first elute nonpolar impurities rapidly without moving polar target compounds, and then progressively increase solvent strength to elute more polar components cleanly.

options.label: C
options.text: To measure the boiling point of the fractions.

options.label: D
options.text: To destroy the silica gel packing.

questions.correct_answer: To first elute nonpolar impurities rapidly without moving polar target compounds, and then progressively increase solvent strength to elute more polar components cleanly.
questions.explanation: Starting with nonpolar eluent resolves fast-moving components; gradually increasing polarity provides sufficient eluting power to desorb and isolate polar fractions.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.question: What is the chemical function of adding anhydrous magnesium sulfate (MgSO₄) to an organic extraction layer prior to solvent evaporation?

options.label: A
options.text: It forms insoluble crystalline hydrates (MgSO₄·7H₂O), removing residual dissolved and suspended microscopic water droplets from the organic solvent.

options.label: B
options.text: It oxidizes secondary alcohols to ketones.

options.label: C
options.text: It dissolves all organic impurities.

options.label: D
options.text: It neutralizes excess organic bases.

questions.correct_answer: It forms insoluble crystalline hydrates (MgSO₄·7H₂O), removing residual dissolved and suspended microscopic water droplets from the organic solvent.
questions.explanation: Anhydrous inorganic salts coordinate water into solid crystal hydrates, rendering the organic extract completely dry.

questions.chapter_title: A Review of General Chemistry: Electrons, Bonds, and Molecular Properties
questions.topic: Acid-Base Extraction of Carboxylic Acid and Phenol
questions.question: In an organic laboratory separation of benzoic acid (pKa 4.2), 4-tert-butylphenol (pKa 10.2), and naphthalene in diethyl ether, what reagent selectively extracts ONLY benzoic acid into the aqueous layer?

options.label: A
options.text: 6 M Aqueous hydrochloric acid (HCl).

options.label: B
options.text: Saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate (5% NaHCO₃, pH ~ 8), which deprotonates strong benzoic acid but is too weak to deprotonate phenol.

options.label: C
options.text: Concentrated aqueous NaOH (pH 14).

options.label: D
options.text: Distilled deionized water.

questions.correct_answer: Saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate (5% NaHCO₃, pH ~ 8), which deprotonates strong benzoic acid but is too weak to deprotonate phenol.
questions.explanation: Weak base NaHCO₃ (pKa of H₂CO₃ = 6.35) selectively deprotonates carboxylic acids (pKa ~ 4–5) without deprotonating phenols (pKa ~ 10).
